q-43343.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266178/assets/192cd7673f9186480bd6ab9955e56eab78b8a4e3bbec9d8d824922b5fd9c0527.png)

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{15\sqrt{3}}{2}{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Determine $m∠A.$
q-43343.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=5\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC=6\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $m∠A$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{15\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 6\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{15\sqrt{3}}{2} & =15\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{\cancel{15}\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\cancel{15}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡A & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ m∠A & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

The area of ​​the triangle △ABC is 1532 cm2. Determine m∠A.

a
50∘
b
45∘
c
65∘
d
75∘
e
60∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the area of the triangle is A=12bcsin⁡A, where ∠A is between the sides of lengths b and c.

Here, we have c=AB=5 cm,b=AC=6 cm.

Therefore, we can calculate m∠A as follows:

A=12⋅b⋅c⋅sin⁡A1532=12⋅5⋅6⋅sin⁡A1532=15⋅sin⁡A1532=15⋅sin⁡Asin⁡A=32m∠A=60∘.

q-72756.name: Question 2
q-72756.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266178/assets/721f8231c38ba5937b4e2f80233f83ecb52605388897291d14968064f214a4c4.png)

Rounded to the nearest tenth, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$
q-72756.worked_solution:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $△ABD$ and $△BDC$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266178/assets/2bdf5043e8bd25884eeda042c276fad2e5fa267e1f9f19d9271564576965d09a.png)

 

First we find the area for $△ABD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 10\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{110}^{∘} \\  & =30\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{110}^{∘} \\  & ≈28.190\,7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Now we find the area for $△BCD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{BDC} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 13\cdot 15\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{58}^{∘} \\  & =97.5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{58}^{∘} \\  & ≈82.684\,7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & ={A}_{ABD}+{A}_{BDC} \\  & =28.190\,7+82.684\,7 \\  & =110.875\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, to the nearest tenth, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $110.9.$

Question 2
?

Rounded to the nearest tenth, what is the area of the quadrilateral ABCD?

a
98.7
b
110.9
c
112.6
d
77.4
e
102.7
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The area of the quadrilateral ABCD is the sum of the areas of the triangles △ABD and △BDC (see the illustration below).

First we find the area for △ABD: AABD=12⋅6⋅10⋅sin⁡110∘=30⋅sin⁡110∘≈28.1907, rounded to four decimal places.

Now we find the area for △BCD: ABDC=12⋅13⋅15⋅sin⁡58∘=97.5⋅sin⁡58∘≈82.6847, rounded to four decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of ABCD: AABCD=AABD+ABDC=28.1907+82.6847=110.8754

Consequently, to the nearest tenth, the area of the quadrilateral ABCD is 110.9.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14266178/assets/f53996727138b9442ac041cf492618db8287b54ba652c4f9e375cdde27dc1862.png)

The area of $ABCD$ is $34{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$   What is the area of $△BCD$ rounded to the nearest integer?
q-72764.worked_solution:
Let's start by finding the area of $△ABD.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot AD\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 9\cdot 15\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{52}^{∘} \\  & =67.5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{52}^{∘} \\  & =53.190… \\  & ≈53{\text{ cm}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of $△ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $△BCD.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△BCD} & ={A}_{△ABD}-{A}_{ABCD} \\  & =53-34 \\  & =19{\text{ cm}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

A△ABD=12⋅AB⋅AD⋅sin⁡A=12⋅9⋅15⋅sin⁡52∘=67.5⋅sin⁡52∘=53.190…≈53 cm2 rounded to the nearest integer.
